topic.title: The monthly toll pass is the expensive plan
topic.claim: The monthly plan is the one built for people who don't want to think about it, and that is what makes it the costly one.
topic.behaviour: We pick the small monthly payment because it hurts less today, even when a yearly option is much cheaper. It happens with toll passes, gym plans and streaming subscriptions.
topic.mechanism: A small recurring amount rarely gets reviewed, and inertia pays the seller for years. The yearly plan asks for thought and money upfront, so many people skip it even when it saves more.
topic.group: Daily commuters and people with a stack of subscriptions
topic.moment: You have paid the same small amount every month for so long that you have stopped looking at the number.

turn.believed: A monthly plan is the safe and flexible choice.
turn.actually: Monthly is the price of not paying attention. The seller earns from your habit, not your need.

topic.feeling: slightly foolish, and wondering what else is on auto-pay
topic.villain: a subscription model that rewards the customer who stops checking
topic.because: Sellers earn more from the monthly option because most customers renew without comparing. Yearly options exist, but they require you to do the maths once.

proof.fact: From 1 November 2026, eligible private vehicle owners living within 20 km of a National Highway fee plaza can buy an annual FASTag local pass at ₹1,500 or ₹3,000, while the monthly local pass costs ₹360, or ₹4,320 a year, so the annual pass can save ₹2,820.

topic.payoff: Open your auto-pay list tonight and check which ones you would sign up for again today. The rest are paying for your habit.
topic.send_to: The friend with seven subscriptions who says they 'barely notice' the charges.
real_details: Living nearby does not automatically qualify you; the pass is not available on closed-toll expressways or where a service road exists.
topic.news_peg: Annual FASTag local pass rules effective 2026-11-01, reported 2026-10-28
topic.why_now: The new pass has just started, and it is a clear example of paying more to avoid thinking.

sources.fact: From 1 Nov 2026, residents within 20 km of an NH toll plaza can buy a local annual FASTag pass at Rs 1,500 a year outside municipal or local town limits and Rs 3,000 within them. The standard annual pass costs Rs 3,075 in 2026-27. The page does not give the monthly pass price, so it does not show that the monthly plan costs more.

NHAI, announced by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, revised the FASTag annual pass fee from Rs 3,000 to Rs 3,075 for FY 2026-27. It covers one year or 200 toll plaza crossings, whichever comes first.
sources.excerpt: The pass is a one-time payment that covers either one year of validity or 200 toll plaza crossings, whichever comes first

cover.headline: The monthly plan is the one built for [people who stopped checking]
cover.sub: It feels flexible. You're just paying extra for it every month.

paragraphs: The monthly plan was never the flexible option. It's the one made for people who stopped checking.
slides.why_swipe: Isn't monthly the safe choice? Why would it be the costly one?

paragraphs: Almost every seller has a yearly plan too. It's cheaper, but it makes you sit down and do the maths once.
The monthly plan never asks you to think. Not on day one, not in year three.
slides.why_swipe: Where does this show up in my own bank statement?

paragraphs:
This is why:
– the gym plan you've paid for since the January you meant it
– the OTT app you joined for one show, two seasons ago
– the cloud storage still backing up a phone you sold
slides.why_swipe: And why don't I notice any of it?

paragraphs: The bank SMS says "Debited." You swipe it away mid-meeting without reading the amount.
"It's only ₹199, yaar." Said every month, for years.
slides.why_swipe: How much is that small amount really costing?

paragraphs: The new FASTag local pass, live since 1 November, has both plans on one price list.
Monthly: ₹360, so ₹4,320 a year. Annual, outside town limits: ₹1,500 once. That's ₹2,820 less.
slides.why_swipe: So why does the small number win anyway?

paragraphs: A small charge never gets a second look. So it renews on autopilot, month after month.
For an app or a gym, that's the easiest customer there is: one who stopped checking.
slides.why_swipe: Then why do smart people keep choosing monthly?

paragraphs: ₹199 is too small to feel like a decision, so it never gets one. They won you once. They never have to again.
slides.why_swipe: So is there any upside to monthly at all?

paragraphs: I get why monthly wins. You never see the full price.
slides.why_swipe: So what is sitting on my own auto-pay list?

paragraphs: Open your auto-pay list. Keep what you'd sign up for again today. The rest is just billing your habit.
The seller doesn't need you to want it. Only to stop checking.

end.save: Come back to this the next time a ₹199 charge shows up and you don't remember why.
end.send: Send to the friend with seven subscriptions who swears they barely notice the charges.
end.promise: Where your money really goes in India.

draft.caption: We'll argue for ten minutes over a ₹40 delivery fee and never look at the ₹199 that left this month.
draft.alt_text: A text reel of nine plain cards arguing that monthly plans are built for people who stop checking. It says the yearly plan asks you to do the maths once while monthly never asks you to think, and lists a gym plan, an OTT app and old cloud storage as examples. It describes swiping away a bank debit SMS mid-meeting without reading the amount. It uses the new FASTag local pass, ₹360 a month or ₹4,320 a year against a ₹1,500 annual pass outside town limits, to show a ₹2,820 gap. It says small charges never feel like a decision, so the seller wins you once and never has to again, admits monthly wins because you never see the full price, and ends by telling you to keep only what you'd sign up for again today, since the seller only needs you to stop checking.

claims.text: The FASTag local pass rules took effect on 1 November 2026.
The monthly FASTag local pass costs ₹360, or ₹4,320 a year, for eligible owners.
The annual FASTag local pass costs ₹1,500 a year for eligible residents outside municipal or local town limits.
Paying once for the ₹1,500 annual pass instead of monthly costs ₹2,820 less.
